notes: RETROSPECTIVE, not pre-registered: built after the election with the result and market resolutions known. Settings were chosen on the 2022 and 2019 count nights replayed from the same AEC archive in feed order; no 2025 count went into them.

Two model versions are shown. v1 is the headline (solid line). v2 is a sensitivity (thin dashed line). It was written after v1 had been scored on the 2025 count and its misses looked at. Its settings still come only from 2022 and 2019.

The map has 150 divisions, on the 2025 boundaries. The count is replayed from the AEC's own election-night feed: 365 messages, each used from the time the AEC created it. Times are Canberra time (AEST). The first two-candidate count came at 18:33. The last message shown is 02:37.
'Counted' is the share of votes counted at polling places, measured against what the same places counted last time. Postal, absent and provisional votes come in later. They are not in the night feed.

The map shows Labor's share of the two-party vote (Labor against the Coalition). In about 20 divisions the real contest was not Labor against the Coalition. The 'winning party' view shows the real winner of each division.

How the model works: it finds the swing in the polling places already counted. It compares each place with the same place at the last election. It blends that swing with the swing in the state and in the country. The winner of each division is the candidate ahead after preferences. The AEC picks the two candidates for that count. In 21 divisions its pick was wrong all night. There the model uses the Labor against Coalition count and the first-preference leaders. 8,000 random draws turn this into seat counts.

Questions modelled: most seats, majority, hung parliament, Labor and Coalition seat bands, the Labor minus Coalition seat gap, Greens 4 or more, and four seat markets (Dickson, Grayndler, Bennelong, Brisbane). Prime minister questions are modelled as 'the party with the most seats gets the prime minister'. The count cannot test that in a hung parliament. Not modelled: minority governments, other prime minister names, the national first-preference vote, and small parties.
The model was too sure of itself. Labor's final seat count was inside its 90% range in only 10% of minutes (v1) and 79% (v2). Read 'the model was sure first' with that in mind.
Final seats (AEC): Labor 94, Coalition 43, Greens 1, others 12. Labor's final two-party share: 55.22%.

Evidence: RETROSPECTIVE, not pre-registered: built after the election with the result and market resolutions known. Settings were chosen on the 2022 and 2019 count nights replayed from the same AEC archive in feed order; no 2025 count went into them.

sensitivities.note: Instead of one setting for how wrong the early count can be, the model is run twice, once with the national swing error that the 2019 night needed and once with the one the 2022 night needed (equal weights, the seat draws pooled); the 2025 count and result chose nothing, but the idea was adopted after the result was known.
